item.title: 【Singles (lossless)】WAV - Lil Suzy "When I Fall In Love" US CD Maxi
item.description:
Lil Suzy | When I Fall In Love​

judge me, fight me and/or cancel me but i hated the brief euro-dance craze of the mid-1990s. no, i did not like la bouche’s chart-topping single “be my lover.” i only hum along to real mccoy’s “runaway” because radio played it to nauseam. quite honestly, one of the only euro-dance i liked was gina g’s “ooh aah…just a little bit.”

one other euro-dance song i liked was lil suzy’s “when i fall in love.” i didn’t particularly like it upon its release because i preferred her freestyle songs. the song was in heavy rotation on philadelphia’s q102 and i’d listened to it while it played. hearing anything by a freestyle artist in 1995 on radio made me happy. but i wouldn’t come to like the song until late 1997.

in late 1997, i joined lil suzy’s team as a background dancer and one of the songs we performed was “when i fall in love.”it was the only routine i didn’t choreograph because the song was so damn fast! but it was a fun song to perform and overtime, it became my favorite.

“when i fall in love” proved to have legs at radio. for almost a year, the song would reach a peak in one region before then finding an audience in another city and reach a peak there. this was repeated several times. and because all of this didn’t happen simultaneously, it could not mass enough points to chart on billboard’s hot 100. but it remains one her more popular singles. the song is also a reminder of how lil suzy could successfully pivot from to freestyle to other dance sounds during a time when radio absolutely ignored freestyle music.

item.description:
Wham! 10 Days in China (2026)
1080p.BBCIP.WEB-DL.AAC.2.0.H.264

In 1985, Wham! made history as the first western pop act to perform in communist China. George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley travelled to Beijing and Guangzhou for a series of concerts that would make history. At a time when China was beginning to open to the wider world, their performances represented more than just entertainment - they were a rare cultural exchange and, for the audiences who attended, a first glimpse of western pop music performed live.

Film-maker Lindsay Anderson had been commissioned to document the tour, but the project was fraught with challenges, leading to Anderson's dismissal. Though a version of the film was released, most of the footage was largely unseen. Using digitised archival footage alongside interviews with those who were there, this film presents a vivid portrait of a tour that has become legendary. It captures intimate moments behind the scenes, the nuanced political context, the excitement of the performances and the bizarre twists and turns of a true story that is stranger than fiction.

Top of the Pops - The Story of: 2000, 2001, 2002 & 2003
1080p.BBCIP.WEB-DL.AAC.2.0.H.264



Top of the Pops - The Story of 2000

Top of the Pops officially enters the new millennium. In a year that saw the highest number of individual number ones, dance music is on the rise (again) thanks to the boom in filesharing, helping DJs such as Sonique and Spiller top the charts. Craig David takes a seemingly permanent residence in the Top 10, whilst pop continues to dominate not just the chart but TV sets too, with S Club back for their second album and second TV series. American hip-hop is on the rise, whilst the show still has room for more eclectic bands such as Eels.
Contributors include Craig David, Sonique, S Club, Spiller, Darude, Scott Robinson from 5ive, Eels' Mark 'E' Everett and broadcasters Trevor Nelson, Pete Tong and Sarah Cawood.

Top of the Pops - The Story of 2001

A year into the new millennium, Top of the Pops is bigger, brighter and faster. Guitar bands bring their A-game to the show, from mosh pit megastars Feeder to Wheatus's frat-rock jives and The Dandy Warhols' bohemian vibes. Shaggy returns with RikRok with the best-selling single of the year - and an anthem for flat denial. ITV's new talent show produces Hear'Say, Gorillaz graces the studio in virtual form, and the show witnesses the dawn of grime when So Solid Crew come to collect their crown.
The new boyband of the year are Blue, and at the end of the year, Robbie and Nicole Kidman take the Christmas number one - but it's a studio singalong with Jocelyn Brown that rounds the year off with the heartfelt song of hope War Is Over. Contributors include Grant Nicholas and Taka Hirose of Feeder, Shaggy, Ricky 'RikRok' Ducent, Lisa Maffia of So Solid Crew, Brendan B Brown of Wheatus, Simon Webbe, Anthony Costa, Lee Ryan and Duncan James of Blue, and Courtney Taylor-Taylor and Zia McCabe of The Dandy Warhols.

Top of the Pops - The Story of 2002

A look back at a year where Top of the Pops comes under attack from the TV talent show and girl groups are back at the top. 2002 sees the return of Sugababes 2.0, the chart domination of talent show winners (and losers), as well as the cultural phenomenon which is Vanessa Carlton with that piano riff.
Meanwhile, Swedish band The Hives arrive at Television Centre, whilst indie rock continues its early 00s climb of the chart. With 2,000 episodes under its belt, TOTP is more diverse and dominant than ever before.
Contributors include Mutya and Keisha from Sugababes, Kimberly Walsh from Girls Aloud, Vanessa Carlton, Liberty X, The Hives, Frankie Bridge from S Club Juniors, Gareth Gates and broadcasters Trevor Nelson, Pete Tong and Sarah Cawood.

Top of the Pops - The Story of 2003

2003 was a year of wall-to-wall bangers. If it was belting, we were buying! Forget music trends - nobody was sticking to the rules. Pop was punky, with Busted breaking the mould. Bhangra was funky, as Panjabi MC launched a monster hit with Mundian To Bach Ke - and Jay-Z jumped on with a remix to make yet another hit. R&B loved an emcee in our brightest girl band Mis-Teeq. Guitar bands ruled, as stadium rockers The Darkness staked their claim for greatness, The Libertines arrived as the post punk poets of Albion, and Electric Six landed from Detroit with their fuzzed-up, high octane and high camp disco rock.
Beyoncé ruled the summer with her first solo single, and all year long the chart was a race for those fresh from the stable of ITV's Popstars and BBC's Fame Academy, but it was Girls Aloud who romped to victory as the clear favourites. As the world's biggest music show was relaunched into an all-new era, Chris Cowey bowed out after six years at the helm and Andi Peters returned to the BBC as Top of the Pops head honcho, bringing a new theme, new graphics and a new presenter in Tim Kash. Exclusive performances and future hits were key to the all-new TOTP, and an extended show was launched on the new BBC Three with added spice.
The race for Christmas number one was lit with The Darkness's Don't Let the Bells End as the clear contender, before Gary Jules and Michael Andrews pipped them to the post with a cover of Tears for Fears' Mad World, rounding off the year on a melancholic note.
Contributors include Matt Willis and Charlie Simpson of Busted, Panjabi MC, Sabrina Washington of Mis-Teeq, Carl Barat and Peter Doherty of The Libertines, Justin Hawkins of The Darkness, Kimberley Walsh of Girls Aloud and Dick Valentine of Electric Six.
